title: POC scoping - Private networking & data residency - Harbor Health
next_steps: Sofia to share draft SOW and pilot pricing
Harbor to send VPC diagram and account IDs for PrivateLink/VPC peering evaluation
Schedule benchmark run (model + workload) week of 2026-04-06
Sofia/Liam to share security pack and SOC2 artifacts
action_items: Sofia Martinez - Send draft SOW and pilot pricing by 2026-04-02
Maya Lin - Share VPC/network diagram and list of allowed egress CIDRs by 2026-04-01
Liam O'Neill - Prepare benchmark plan and dataset, propose model variants by 2026-04-03

summary: Initial POC scoping with Harbor Health focused on private networking (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), data residency requirements across US regions, workload sizing and benchmark criteria. Agreed success criteria (latency/throughput and data controls), action items and timeline for a 4-6 week pilot with network prep and benchmark run in early April.
topics: Private networking: VPC peering vs AWS PrivateLink
Workload sizing: qps, concurrency, token budgets
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Martinez: Thanks everyone for joining, we're excited to scope this POC for Harbor Health. I'm Sofia, AE on the account, and Liam from our infra team will drive the technical side.
[00:07] Rajesh Patel: Great thanks, Sofia. Quick intros - I'm Rajesh, CTO. Maya runs infra, Tomas is security lead, Emily on product, Jordan on ML.
[00:16] Liam O'Neill: Hey all - quick overview from our side: the POC we typically run for private networking includes a short network hookup (VPC peering or PrivateLink), a benchmark against your workload shape, and a residency verification.
[00:28] Maya Lin: Our main constraint is that PHI must not leave us regionally - so US only endpoints, preferably us-east-1. We also have egress rules that only allow traffic to specific partner IPs.
[00:40] Tomas Alvarez: We'll need full audit logs, KMS integration for any key material, and SOC2 artifacts. Also want to confirm that the inference nodes are not writing logs to third-party storage without explicit control.
[00:52] Sofia Martinez: Totally. For Private mode we support a customer-managed VPC option and can do either VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink. VPC peering is lower complexity for internal-only traffic, but PrivateLink gives you more control over egress and avoids route table changes.
[01:06] Rajesh Patel: Which one is recommended for a hospital-grade environment? We want minimal blast radius and clear egress paths.
[01:12] Liam O'Neill: For hospitals we often recommend PrivateLink when you have strict egress allowlists and don't want cross-account route propagation. PrivateLink uses ENIs in your VPC and you only need to allow our service IPs. If you prefer full L3 connectivity and lower per-request cost, peering can work but requires more careful routing.
[01:28] Maya Lin: Cost isn't the primary concern, it's isolation and auditable paths. PrivateLink sounds appealing. What IP ranges or endpoints do you provide?
[01:36] Sofia Martinez: We'll provide a short list of service endpoints per region and a maintained set of CIDR blocks. For the pilot we'll give a transient allowlist. Liam, can you confirm the exact artifacts we send?
[01:43] Liam O'Neill: Yes - network diagram, endpoint DNS names, IP ranges, and recommended security group rules. We'll also include a step-by-step for setting up interface endpoints.
[01:52] Jordan Park: On the ML side our workload is a mix of short chat responses and longer document summarization. Expected 40 RPS peak across 6 concurrent services, average 350 tokens in/out for summaries and 60 tokens for chat. Latency p95 under 700ms for chat and p95 under 2.5s for summarization is ideal.
[02:12] Sofia Martinez: That's useful - helps us pick model families and instance sizing. Do you have a target cost per 1k requests or per 1M tokens that we should aim for?
[02:20] Rajesh Patel: Not a hard target, but we want to ensure unit economics don't balloon - ballpark under $0.50 per 1k small-chat interactions and under $5 per 1k long summaries would be acceptable.
[02:31] Liam O'Neill: We'll run two benchmark profiles: chat profile (60 tokens, 40 qps, 6 concurrency) and summarization profile (350 tokens, 8 qps, burst concurrency 4). We'll measure p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, and cost estimates across model variants (full float vs quantized).
[02:48] Emily Rhodes: For success criteria, product needs consistency - no more than 5% error in output regressions vs current baseline and latency/throughput targets met for at least 95% of requests.
[02:58] Tomas Alvarez: And security success criteria: traffic must stay inside US regions, keys never leave our KMS, audit logs available to us for 90 days.
[03:08] Sofia Martinez: Understood. We'll propose concrete SLI thresholds in the SOW but summarizing now: (1) network established via PrivateLink in us-east-1; (2) benchmark run hitting p95/p99 latency targets; (3) data residency verified; (4) security artifacts provided.
[03:24] Rajesh Patel: Timeline? We have a regulatory review in mid-May so need results before then.
[03:30] Liam O'Neill: We can do a quick 2-week network hookup and baseline benchmark, then a 4-week extended trial if you want deeper evaluation. For your timeline, do the baseline run week of April 6 and a follow-up by early May would fit.
[03:41] Maya Lin: That aligns. We'll need the network details this week to get our infra team to open a change window.
[03:47] Sofia Martinez: Action: we'll send VPC endpoint details and SOW draft by end of day Thursday.
[03:52] Jordan Park: For benchmarks, will you run using our prompts or synthetic ones? We prefer using a small representative corpus with de-identified patient notes.
[03:59] Liam O'Neill: We can run with your de-identified corpus. We'll coordinate on secure transfer - S3 presigned link to your PrivateLink-accessible bucket or sftp into our isolated benchmark env. We'll make sure any artifact is ephemeral and deleted after the run.
[04:13] Tomas Alvarez: Confirm that the presigned link won't be accessible from outside our VPC and that logs about the transfer are available.
[04:18] Liam O'Neill: Yes we'll lock the bucket to the interface endpoint and share transfer logs.
[04:23] Emily Rhodes: Any constraints on region pinning? We want all inference in us-east-1 but ingest from us-west-2 for redundancy.
[04:31] Sofia Martinez: We can pin inference to us-east-1. For ingest cross-region, we'll propose a routing policy - primary us-east-1 with failover to us-west-2 only if explicitly allowed. We'll document egress behavior in the SOW.
[04:43] Rajesh Patel: Are there any regulatory issues with PrivateLink + cross-region ingest?
[04:48] Tomas Alvarez: As long as inference stays in-region and logs/audit trail are clear, cross-region ingest can be allowed. We need to ensure backups or debug dumps don't cross borders.
[04:57] Liam O'Neill: We'll include a runbook that shows where artifacts land and retention controls.
[05:02] Sofia Martinez: On quantization and model variants - to hit your latency goals we might propose a quantized 4-bit variant for summarization and full fp16 for chat. That usually cuts per-token compute by ~2-3x with small quality tradeoffs.
[05:16] Jordan Park: We'll want an A/B check - make sure QA sign-off on summaries before rolling out.
[05:21] Emily Rhodes: Can you do canary rollouts and automatic fallback to hosted if latencies spike?
[05:26] Liam O'Neill: Yes - Redwood's rollout supports canary, AB, and automatic fallback to a lower-cost hosted model or an alternate region. We can include that in the pilot config.
[05:36] Rajesh Patel: Any additional networking changes required on our side for PrivateLink?
[05:41] Liam O'Neill: Minimal: create an interface endpoint in your VPC, attach security groups allowing outbound to our service, and add a resolver rule if you need private DNS. We'll provide exact commands.
[05:53] Maya Lin: Ok please include terraform snippets if possible - those speed up our change approvals.
[05:58] Sofia Martinez: We'll attach terraform and CloudFormation snippets in the SOW repo.
[06:02] Tomas Alvarez: On KMS - we need to use our own CMKs for any customer key material. Is that supported?
[06:09] Liam O'Neill: Yes, we integrate with customer-managed KMS for key wrapping and we can accept HSM-backed keys for Private deployments. We'll document the key exchange and rotation policy.
[06:20] Sofia Martinez: Recap of next steps and timeline: send SOW + network artifacts by Thursday, baseline benchmark week of 2026-04-06, security checklist due 2026-04-05, and follow-up call to review results the week of 2026-04-13.
[06:38] Rajesh Patel: Sounds good. Any blockers from Redwood side?
[06:42] Liam O'Neill: None; main dependency is getting your VPC diagram and account IDs so we can provision the interface endpoint and plan the benchmark.
[06:51] Maya Lin: We'll get that out by end of day Wednesday.
[06:54] Sofia Martinez: Great - thanks everyone. We'll capture action items and share meeting notes and the SOW link.
[07:00] Emily Rhodes: Thank you, talk soon.
[07:03] [call ends]
